_comment: Evaluation questions. `expect` lists substrings that a relevant chunk should contain; a question is satisfied when a retrieved chunk contains any of them (two, for chunks over 500 chars - see run_eval.is_relevant). This is cheaper to maintain than chunk-ID labels, which change on every re-index. Questions marked "hard": true are deliberately chosen to be losable - they paraphrase the archive rather than quoting it, or target a topic mentioned in only one or two chunks. The easy set saturated at recall@5 1.00, which hid regressions rather than proving quality; these exist so the metric can move. `unanswerable` holds questions the archive genuinely cannot answer. The "near" ones are UK student topics that simply never came up (re-verified against the 2017-2025 corpus - three earlier entries had to be replaced once the archive widened and began covering them) - a harder and more realistic decline than another country, which the wording alone gives away.
